## Employee
- Name: Gandu (no id)
- Role: Instrumentation Engineer, Instrumentation
- Plant / unit: Haldia  / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Undocumented Instrumentation Quirks in Unit 300
topics.rationale: No equipment records exist for this profile, so the most valuable knowledge is the unwritten gotchas and workarounds the engineer carries in their head.
seed_questions: Which instrument in Unit 300 has a personality of its own that no manual ever captured?
What is the one loop or device that only you know how to keep running, and what's the trick?
Are there any 'ghost' alarms or readings that everyone learns to ignore but are never documented?

topics.title: Key Instrumentation Assets and Their Hidden Histories
topics.rationale: Since the knowledge graph has no equipment linked to this engineer, we must start by having them name the most critical or troublesome instruments they owned.
seed_questions: Which 5-10 field instruments or control systems in Unit 300 have consumed most of your time over the years?
For each, what is the one failure mode that keeps coming back despite documented fixes?
Are there any instruments with known calibration drift patterns that aren't in the CMMS?

topics.title: Unfinished Instrumentation Projects and Loose Ends
topics.rationale: Retiring engineers often leave behind half-finished upgrades, trials, or root-cause investigations that exist only in their notebooks or memory.
seed_questions: What instrumentation improvement projects did you start but never fully close out?
Are there any temporary fixes or bypasses still in place that were meant to be permanent solutions?
Which vendor trials or new technology evaluations were underway and need a decision?

topics.title: Vendor and Spare Parts Tribal Knowledge
topics.rationale: Knowing which vendor rep to call, which spare part is actually interchangeable, and which 'equivalent' part will fail is critical and rarely written down.
seed_questions: Which instrument vendors have given us persistent quality issues that aren't reflected in the approved vendor list?
Who are your go-to technical contacts at key suppliers, and what's the backchannel to get urgent support?
Are there any 'will-fit' spare parts you use that aren't in the official BOM but work better?

topics.title: Critical Safety Instrumented System (SIS) Insights
topics.rationale: SIS testing and bypass procedures often have practical nuances that deviate from the written SOPs, especially during plant upsets.
seed_questions: During a Unit 300 trip or SIS activation, what manual interventions have you performed that aren't in the cause-and-effect diagrams?
Are there any SIS test procedures where the written steps are impractical or unsafe, and what did you actually do?
Which safety instrumented functions have the longest history of spurious trips, and what was the real root cause?

topics.title: Control Loop Tuning and Advanced Process Control (APC) Secrets
topics.rationale: Optimal tuning parameters for difficult loops are often stored only in the engineer's personal files or head, especially for surge or interacting loops.
seed_questions: Which control loops in Unit 300 have tuning parameters that you've tweaked over the years and never updated in the DCS documentation?
Are there any APC applications that are running in a degraded mode with manual overrides you've been managing?
What is the one loop that operators constantly switch to manual, and what's the underlying instrumentation issue?

topics.title: Role Evolution and Unwritten Responsibilities
topics.rationale: The formal job description rarely captures the full scope of what a long-tenured engineer actually does, especially during turnarounds and emergencies.
seed_questions: Beyond your official Instrumentation Engineer duties, what tasks or areas did you unofficially own because you were the only one who knew them?
During a Unit 300 turnaround, what is your personal checklist that isn't in the standard work package?
What cross-discipline issues (e.g., mechanical, process) did you routinely help troubleshoot because of your instrumentation perspective?

topics.title: Obsolescence and Upgrade Battle Scars
topics.rationale: Legacy systems in a plant like Haldia often have painful upgrade histories, including failed cutovers and compatibility issues known only to the veteran engineer.
seed_questions: Which legacy instrumentation systems in Unit 300 are held together by sheer willpower, and what is the exact failure risk?
Have there been any failed upgrade or migration attempts on DCS, PLC, or field instruments that we should never repeat?
What is the most critical obsolete part for which you've been hoarding a personal stash?

topics.title: Handover Advice and Open Risks for Successor
topics.rationale: A dedicated handover topic ensures the successor gets a prioritized list of risks and immediate actions, not just a data dump.
seed_questions: If you had only one week with your replacement, what are the top 3 things you would physically show them in the field?
What is the single biggest instrumentation risk that could shut down Unit 300 in the next 6 months, and what's the early warning sign?
Which shift team or operator has the best instinct for instrumentation problems, and who should your successor build a relationship with first?

topics.title: Turnaround and Shutdown Instrumentation Scope Gaps
topics.rationale: The standard turnaround instrumentation scope often misses critical inspections or tests that the experienced engineer adds informally.
seed_questions: What instrumentation checks do you always add to the turnaround scope that aren't in the official plan?
Which critical instruments require a specific technician or vendor specialist during shutdowns, and why?
Are there any interlock bypasses or overrides you routinely manage during startup that a new engineer would not know to look for?

topics.title: Process-Equipment-Instrumentation Interaction Anomalies
topics.rationale: The most dangerous failures often occur at the intersection of process conditions and instrument limitations, a domain where only experience reveals the pattern.
seed_questions: What process condition (e.g., a specific feedstock, weather, rate change) has historically caused instrumentation to give false readings or fail in Unit 300?
Are there any 'impossible' readings that operators report which you've learned actually indicate a real, specific upstream problem?
Which analyzer or measurement is the least trusted by operations, and what is the real accuracy story?

topics.title: Documentation Gaps and Personal Knowledge Repositories
topics.rationale: Critical information often resides in personal notebooks, marked-up drawings, or email folders that will be lost upon departure.
seed_questions: Where do you keep your personal notes, marked-up P&IDs, or loop folders that are not on the shared drive?
Which official documentation (e.g., instrument datasheets, wiring diagrams) do you know contains errors, and what are the corrections?
Is there a 'cheat sheet' or quick-reference guide you made for yourself that your successor absolutely needs a copy of?
